text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx + timeouts for /api/v1/generate in prod-us-west-2. 5xx rate ~12% (baseline 0.5%), p95 latency x3. Runbook 'batcher-congestion' auto-triggered. alert_id=A-3242109876

jordan: I'm on it — pulling up Console dashboards (https://console.redwood/ops/dashboards/3242109876). Any recent deploys?

sam: no deploys in last 60m. Looking at scheduler metrics: batcher queue depth for pool `scheduler-pool-7` jumped from ~300 -> ~18k in ~9m. continuous-batcher latency exploding. KV-cache miss rate up 4x. Tail latency > 10s, timeouts showing up at the gateway.

lee: gateway logs show a lot of 502/504 proxied from runtime-batcher. Could be head-of-line: a few long-context requests blocking batch windows. Any large context requests spiking?

emily: grep of logs for long-context requests: found many requests with context > 32k tokens from a single client IP range (34.78.12.0/24) starting at 3242109500. Possible bot or mis-specified client.

sam: correlating request ids -> these long requests are getting stuck waiting for KV warmup inside the batcher. Batcher is attempting to assemble huge continuous batches and starving short-request traffic.

lee: runbook step 1 = reduce batch window on pool-7 and scale up. I'm going to change batching config to 30ms and scale nodes.

emily: executing scale now:
```bash
# scale batcher pool
kubectl -n runtime scale deployment batcher-pool-7 --replicas=6
# apply shorter batch window
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap batcher-config -p '{"data":{"batch_window_ms":"30"}}'
```
output:
```
deployment.apps/batcher-pool-7 scaled
configmap/batcher-config patched
```

sam: also temporarily enable per-tenant route fallback to rdx-v1-small for non-enterprise routes to shed load. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl routes update --selector "tier!=enterprise" --model rdx-v1-small --reason "emergency shed - pool-7 congestion"
```

oncall-bot: paging oncall (PD) to primary schedule due to customer impact. PD incidents created: PD-6781, PD-6782.

sophia: customer-impact summary: multiple customers reporting request failures & timeouts (acct-4312, acct-9901). Support already triaging. SLA risk for one mid-market customer (acct-4312) — potential escalation.

jordan: good catch, @sophia. I'm pinging acct-eng for acct-4312 and escalating support to priority. I'm going to handoff — I need to step out for ~20m. @sophia please take lead while I'm out. notes: scaled pool -> 6, batch_window 30ms, fallback routes enabled.

sophia: taking over. I'll monitor metrics and logs. First look: after scale+config change, queue depth dropped from 18k -> 2.1k in ~4m. 5xx rate down from 12% -> 1.8%, p95 latency down by ~60%.

emily: confirming KV-cache warmup actions: we also enabled prefix-level KV warming for hot keys. Patch applied:
```json
{"kv_warm_enabled":"true","kv_warm_prefixes":["/acct/4312","/acct/9901"]}
```
Note: warming will add CPU but reduces runtime stall on first token.

sam: follow-up: we should throttle or block the suspicious IP range (34.78.12.0/24) and contact that tenant. Running ACL now.

lee: ACL applied at edge load balancer to droplist that /24 for write/generate endpoints. Observed immediate reduction in new long-context submissions.

oncall-bot: update: alert A-3242109876 -> status: mitigation_in_progress.

sophia: current status: system degrading -> stabilizing. Active mitigations: pool scale, batch_window shortened, route fallback, KV warm, ACL for offending IP. Customer impact reduced but still seeing intermittent timeouts for a small subset. Support notified and CS on standby.

jordan: quick checklist for post-incident follow-ups (for postmortem):
- throttle controls: add automated detection for long-context request bursts
- safer defaults: cap max batching window for pool-7-like configs
- burst routing: automatic fallback to smaller models when queue depth > threshold
- alert tuning: add runbook step to auto-scale before paging
- contact and verify acct-4312 & acct-9901 status

emily: I've captured commands + timestamps in the incident artifact (s3://redwood-incidents/3242109876/).

sophia: handoff note: i'm monitoring for 30m, will escalate to eng-sre if 5xx >3% for >10m. Leaving this thread open.

oncall-bot: (automated) timeline entry: 3242109876 ALERT -> 3242109500 long-context spike -> 3242109600 scale started -> 3242109850 ACL applied -> 3242110200 5xx reduced.

jordan: thanks team. I trust @sophia and @emily on follow-ups. I'll update postmortem once stable. :thumbsup:

sophia: closing loop for now, moving to incident-triage channel for postmortem planning.
